title: Late-arriving tokens & idempotent-retry accounting: attribution and quota correctness
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Investigate and fix cases where tokens generated after client reconnects or retries are double-billed, mis-attributed to the wrong request, or counted outside the original quota window. This ticket covers both streaming and non-streaming RPC flows, client-side idempotency keys, server-side reconnects, and brokered routing in Dedicated/Private deployments. The root causes appear to be race conditions between the streaming sink finalization step and the metering pipeline commit, plus missing linkage between retry idempotency keys and billing context in the gateway layer.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a streaming generation request with a high token budget (e.g., max_tokens=2048) and capture the session id from the gateway logs.
2) Interrupt the TCP connection mid-stream (simulate flaky network).
3) Immediately resend the same request with a client-provided idempotency_key and allow the server to resume using reconnect semantics.

4) Observe billing records: in the current system the original session's partial tokens are sometimes billed when the client reconnects, and the resumed stream also emits tokens that get billed again or are billed to a new internal request id.
5) Repeat with non-streaming calls where the client retries after a timeout; sometimes the backend accepted the first attempt but the gateway retried leading to duplicate metering entries.
observed_behavior: Duplicate or orphaned token entries in the metering DB; token counts in cost reports exceeding actual application token consumption; quotas unexpectedly tripping after client reconnects; inability to reconcile token totals against request traces in the console. Incidents reported by two customers in the last month (private deploys).
expected_behavior: Each logical user request (defined by client id + idempotency_key or stream session id) maps to a single billing transaction. Tokens emitted on reconnects should be attributed to the original request or merged deterministically and never double-counted. Metering events must be committed atomically with request completion semantics so that partial/aborted streams do not leave orphaned charges.
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a move-commit step in the streaming sink that atomically ties emitted token batches to the metering context only after the gateway acknowledges the session resume or finalization.
2) Propagate client idempotency_key from gateway through broker to runtime and include it on all meter events so they can be deduplicated during ingestion.
3) Add a short tombstone window (30s) for old session ids where late-arriving tokens are accepted but tagged as 'late' and only billed if they correlate with the idempotency_key; otherwise they are dropped.
4) Update metering ingestion to perform idempotency-aware dedupe using (customer_id, idempotency_key, sequence_number) and emit reconciliation records when duplicates are detected.
5) Add end-to-end tests (integration + chaos) that simulate network flaps and gateway retries and assert billing parity against token-level traces.
acceptance_criteria: CI integration test simulating streaming reconnect passes and shows no duplicate billing entries
E2E replay of a previously failing customer incident yields matching token counts and no orphaned metering rows
Console billing dashboard shows corrected per-request token attribution for test runs
Performance regression < 3% on metering ingestion p50 after dedupe changes
Documentation updated: developer docs on idempotency_key propagation and best-practices
comments: 2025-02-21 - Aisha Khan: Initial triage. Found two root causes: gateway not forwarding idempotency_key in reconnect flow; metering commit happens on stream close only which race with reconnect finalization.

2025-02-24 - Marcus Li: Implemented a prototype of idempotency propagation in the gateway, pushed a branch gateway/ENG-4721-idempotency. Added logs to include (customer_id, idempotency_key, session_id) in metering events.
2025-02-26 - SRE (Priya Patel): Chaos test plan reviewed. We'll simulate 6s-30s flaps and broker restarts. Noted disk-backed sink should be resilient to duplicate ingest attempts.

2025-03-01 - Marcus Li: Began changes to metering ingestion pipeline: added a buffered dedupe map keyed by (customer_id, idempotency_key, seq). Running local loadtests to validate memory usage. Observed <2% extra memory under these test loads.

2025-03-03 - Design Review (Lena Moreno): UX in console for 'late tokens' exposure: propose a flag in request detail view showing 'late tokens dropped' with link to trace. Created a follow-up design ticket DES-602.

2025-03-05 - Marcus Li: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/814 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/279 for review. Scheduled performance bench for 2025-03-06. Marking as In Progress.
